response.text:
Good — I won’t make any changes. Below is a concise walkthrough of what moving a recurring “Board prep” meeting from the first Tuesday to the second Tuesday would typically affect in a normal month and what attendees would see.

High-level summary
- Net effect: the meeting shifts one week later each month (from week 1 to week 2). That can create new conflicts with events that already recur on the second Tuesday and may change the timeline for preparing and distributing board materials.
- No action taken here — this is a risk/impact checklist and communications plan you can use before you actually change the series.

What it would commonly “knock into” (categories to check)
1. Recurring meetings that use the second Tuesday
   - Leadership syncs, department reviews, vendor check-ins, or any standing meeting scheduled on “2nd Tuesday.”
   - Weekly meetings that fall on Tuesdays (if attendees have standing weekly events at the same time).
2. Deadlines and prep workflows
   - Internal deadlines for board packet creation/review. If packet deadlines depend on the first-Tuesday timing, you may need to shift those deadlines by a week.
   - Finance/close cycles, legal review windows, or executive approvals that are scheduled relative to the first Tuesday.
3. External constraints
   - Board member travel plans or regularly scheduled external commitments that often land on a mid-month Tuesday.
   - Vendor/partner availability for pre-reads or briefings.
4. Resource bookings
   - Physical room reservations, A/V, and conferencing links that may already be booked on 2nd Tuesdays.
   - Catering or support staff schedules.
5. Time zone and visibility
   - If attendees are in multiple time zones, shifting the date could change daylight-saving relationships in some months (rare but worth checking).
6. Recurrence rules and edge cases
   - How the series was created matters: “first Tuesday” (by ordinal) vs “first business day” vs a date-based recurrence. That affects how calendar systems compute future instances.
   - Months where the first Tuesday and second Tuesday are both in the same calendar week (rarely problematic) or when a second Tuesday falls near holidays.

What attendees would see (immediate calendar UX/behavior)
- Updated invites and notifications
  - If you update the recurring series date, attendees will get an updated invitation (email/calendar notification) showing the new recurring rule and the next occurrence on the second Tuesday.
- Conflict markers
  - Most calendar apps will show a conflict warning or display both events if the new time conflicts with another event already on their calendar. They might have to resolve or move one of the conflicting events.
- RSVP and busy/free
  - The meeting will continue to block time on attendees’ calendars (Busy), and their RSVP status remains unless they respond again.
- Past instances unaffected
  - Prior (past) occurrences remain unchanged. Some calendar systems ask whether to apply the change to “this and future” vs “all events.”
- Per-attendee exceptions
  - If someone has an exception (e.g., they previously declined just the first-Tuesday instance), that exception usually remains for past events but won’t automatically carry to a newly rescheduled series.
- Updated meeting notes/attachments
  - Attachments or links in the recurring invitation will remain; only the date/time recurrence changes unless you edit them.

Checklist before you change the series
- Identify the recurrence rule (first Tuesday by ordinal vs specific dates).
- Search for recurring events on the second Tuesday at the same time (team, executive, HR, finance).
- Confirm board packet production schedule and adjust upstream deadlines if needed.
- Check room and conferencing resource availability for target dates.
- Verify key attendees’ recurring commitments and travel schedules for second Tuesdays.
- Decide how to apply the change: update entire series vs update future occurrences only.
- Prepare a short explanation for attendees (reason and new timeline) and a list of any new deadlines.
- Decide whether to send a calendar update notification or a separate email explaining the change.

Mitigations and suggested approach (if you decide to proceed later)
- Soft step: run a quick availability poll (Doodle/Outlook poll) or propose the change and ask for conflicts before editing the series.
- If conflicts exist, consider keeping a tentative hold on the first-Tuesday slot for one or two months while stakeholders adjust.
- If board packet deadlines are tight, move upstream deadlines first (e.g., draft submission) so the change won’t compress prep time.
- When you update the series: include a clear note in the calendar update explaining why and whether the change applies to future instances only.
- Offer to coordinate room/conference adjustments and confirm resource bookings after the series move.

Questions / next steps (I won’t do anything until you confirm)
- Do you want me to:
  - a) Scan your calendar for likely conflicts on second Tuesdays (requires permission to view calendar), or
  - b) Draft the calendar update message and a short note to attendees explaining the change, or
  - c) Run a proposed-date poll template you can send out?
- Also helpful to know: what time of day is the board prep, is it “monthly on the first Tuesday” by ordinal, and who are the core attendees?

Tell me which next step you want (or give any additional constraints) and I’ll proceed only when you say go.
